word.cultural_note: This is the greeting Muslims have exchanged for over 1,400 years. It's not just a hello — it's a prayer for the other person's wellbeing. The word Islam itself comes from this same root: finding peace through surrendering to God.
word.parent_prompt: Today, try greeting your child with 'Assalamu'alaikum' every time you enter a room. See how many times they respond with 'Wa'alaikumussalam' before bed. Each exchange is a small prayer.
word.ayah_reference: Quran 24:61 — 'When you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from God, blessed and good.'
word.illustration_style: Two figures exchanging a glowing greeting under a starry arch

related_words.note: The name of our faith — finding peace through surrender
A pure heart (qalbun salīm) is a heart at peace

in_the_world: The next time you hear 'Assalamu'alaikum,' notice that you're receiving a gift of peace. You can say it back — and mean it.
